commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Ruby
commitResults.messageBody: Align the Java entry point and user documentation with the Ruby product name, and replace the old Duke output with the selected Big Money-ne startup banner.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add initial Ruby greeting and farewell
commitResults.messageBody: Print the chatbot banner, introduction, prompt, separators, and closing message so the starter application greets the user and exits as required.

commitResults.messageTitle: Echo user commands until bye
commitResults.messageBody: Add a command-reading loop and extract terminal formatting into Ui so Ruby echoes complete input lines, prints a farewell for bye, and exits cleanly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add and list tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Store up to 100 task descriptions, acknowledge newly added tasks, and display the current tasks with one-based numbering while keeping the chatbot active until bye.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mark and unmark tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Represent tasks with completion state, parse one-based mark and unmark commands, and display status icons in numbered task listings and confirmations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add typed tasks for Level 4
commitResults.messageBody: Parse todo, deadline, and event commands into inherited task types and format confirmations and listings according to the required UI output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add project-specific Codex testing skills
commitResults.messageBody: Record exact console UI expectations, add a fail-fast Java 25 test runner, and require UI regression checks after code updates. Include the visual-diff skill so both reusable review workflows are available from the repository.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle invalid commands with Ruby exceptions
commitResults.messageBody: Validate task descriptions, date delimiters, command names, and task numbers so malformed input produces specific recoverable errors without changing task state.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add task deletion with collection storage
commitResults.messageBody: Replace the fixed task array with an ArrayList, support validated delete commands, and verify task removal, counts, and index shifting through UI regression tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Apply Java coding standards
commitResults.messageBody:
Move source files into the ruby package and document public APIs.

Update launch instructions and UI tests for the packaged entry point.

Record Git message limits to prevent future convention violations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Task classes: add disk data format
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks can only display themselves for the user, so nothing
survives a restart.

Storing tasks on disk requires a machine-readable form of each task.

Let's add toDataString() to Task and its subclasses, encoding the type
marker, done flag, description, and dates as a ' | '-separated line,
and a TaskList.toDataString() that joins every task as one line.

commitResults.messageTitle: Persist tasks to data/ruby.txt
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks only exist in memory during a session.

The Level 7 requirement asks that tasks be saved whenever the list
changes and loaded when the chatbot starts.

Let's add a Storage class that reads data/ruby.txt at startup and
rewrites it after every add, mark, unmark, and delete. Ruby now loads
saved tasks before the input loop and saves after each mutation.

While wiring this up, command parsing was extracted from Ruby into a
Parser class so Ruby only dispatches commands and coordinates storage.

commitResults.messageTitle: UI tests: isolate cases and cover storage
commitResults.messageBody:
The new data file persists between runs, so a task added in one
test case would be loaded by the next and break its expected output.

Let's run each test case in its own working directory so saved data
cannot leak between cases, and add two Level 7 cases: one asserts the
data file contents written after add, mark, and delete, and one seeds
the file and verifies the tasks load at startup.

commitResults.messageBody: Add Level 7: save and load tasks from disk

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse task dates as LocalDateTime
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and event dates are stored as raw text, so Ruby cannot
interpret them as real dates or compare them.

The Level 8 requirement asks that dates be understood rather than
treated as opaque strings.

Let's store deadline and event dates as LocalDateTime. Parser now
accepts yyyy-mm-dd or yyyy-mm-dd HHmm input and formats dates as
'Oct 15 2019', appending the time when one was given. Storage reads
and writes dates in ISO format so they survive a restart.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-8: understand dates and times
commitResults.messageBody: Add Level 8: understand dates and times

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor command handling into objects
commitResults.messageBody: Move command parsing and execution out of Ruby so each command\nencapsulates one user action. Ruby now owns its UI, storage,\nand task list, while Storage accepts its file path explicitly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge Level 8 date handling into command objects
commitResults.messageBody:
The command-pattern refactor and the Level 8 LocalDateTime work were
built on the same Level 7 base, so master had one and origin/master had
the other.

Merging origin/master brings both together: commands are parsed into
Command objects, while deadlines and events still store real dates via
Parser.parseDateTime, keeping the 'MMM dd yyyy' display format and ISO
storage format intact.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reorganize sources into ruby sub-packages
commitResults.messageBody:
All classes previously lived in a single flat ruby package, making
it hard to see how the code is organised.

The A-MoreOOP target calls for clearly separated responsibilities.

Let's group the classes by responsibility: command handling in
ruby.command, task types in ruby.task, disk persistence in
ruby.storage, and user interaction in ruby.ui, keeping the entry
point Ruby and RubyException in the ruby root package.

commitResults.messageTitle: build.gradle: point mainClass at ruby.Ruby
Rename shadow jar output to ruby.jar
commitResults.messageBody:
The distributable JAR produced by the shadowJar task is named duke.jar,
a leftover from the upstream Duke starter template.

The chatbot is called Ruby (main class ruby.Ruby), so the JAR name is
misleading.

Let's rename the archive file name to ruby.jar so the build output
matches the project's identity.

The old name is not referenced anywhere else in the repo, so the rename
is safe.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for core classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover the highest-value business logic: parsing, task list
operations, storage round-tripping, and task status transitions.
Document the ~50% coverage target in AGENTS.md and require tests
to be updated after each code change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix import ordering in JUnit tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Static imports should be listed before other imports per the
SE-EDU Java coding standard. ParserTest, StorageTest, TaskListTest,
DeadlineTest, and EventTest listed them after java and org.junit
imports, unlike TaskTest and TodoTest.

Move the static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions imports to the top
of each file so the import order is consistent across the suite.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command for searching tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Users can only list all tasks, so finding a task in a long list
means scanning the whole output by eye.

A find command that matches the keyword against each task's text
makes specific tasks quicker to locate. Matching is
case-insensitive so users need not recall exact casing.

Let's,
* add FindCommand and parse the find keyword in Parser
* search each task's full text in TaskList.find, keeping the
  original list numbering and reporting when nothing matches
* cover find in TaskListTest and ParserTest, and add a Level 9
  section to the UI test plan
